paper_summary: Brown, Carroll, Huddleston, Casias and Long (Sandia, J. Mater. Sci.) study damage mechanisms in elastomeric syntactic foams made of a Sylgard 184 PDMS matrix filled with 3M A16/500 borosilicate glass microballoons at 10, 20, 30, 37 and 46.2 vol%. Cyclic uniaxial compression tests to 60% strain (strain rate 0.15 1/s) are combined with analytic composite theory (Nielsen-Landel solid-sphere equivalent plus Christensen composite spheres) and finite-element homogenisation of RVEs containing 60 GMBs, for undamaged, fully debonded and fully crushed GMB states. The composite bulk modulus collapses when even 5% of the GMBs are crushed while being nearly insensitive to debonding, whereas the shear modulus degrades roughly linearly with crushed fraction and is also reduced by debonding; debonding additionally destroys major symmetry of the homogenised stiffness tensor.

extraction_notes:
This paper contains only two numeric tables: Table 1 (compositions) and Table 2 (constituent elastic constants). Every composite property in the paper - experimental Young's modulus (Fig. 8), predicted bulk/shear moduli vs GMB volume fraction (Figs 3, 4), vs crushed fraction (Fig. 10), vs radius ratio (Fig. 13), and the RVE-size and spacing studies (Figs 14-16) - is presented only as plots, normalised by the neat-matrix value. Per the extraction rules no values were read off those plots, so the five composition records carry composition, processing and test-condition metadata with null moduli.

Unit/format conversions: GMB volume percentages 10, 20, 30, 37, 46.2 -> fractions 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.37, 0.462; GMB weight percentages 1.8, 3.8, 6.3, 9.1, 11.8 -> 0.018, 0.038, 0.063, 0.091, 0.118. Radius ratio eta = ri/ro = 0.9667 is the nominal value stated for the A16 GMBs. Particle true density is not stated in the paper (only the 3M grade name A16/500) and is therefore left null.

The 0.50 densification_strain on the 20 vol% record is the 'around 50% compressive strain' at which the text says a rapid stiffening of the tangent modulus occurs in Fig. 7a (the 20% GMB composite); it is an approximate value stated in the text, not read off the plot, and confidence is lowered accordingly.

Not extracted, with reasons: (1) Table 2 rows for borosilicate glass (E = 61 GPa, K = 32,790 MPa, mu = 25,630 MPa, nu = 0.19) and for the solid-sphere-equivalent GMB phase (K = 1,673 MPa, mu = 2,478 MPa) are constituent/phase properties, not syntactic-foam composite properties, so no records were created for them. (2) All modelled results are quoted as approximate ratios to the neat matrix rather than absolute values - e.g. 'At a GMB volume fraction of 30%, the bulk modulus is approximately 1.2 times higher and the shear modulus is approximately 3 times higher than the neat matrix', 'with 30% GMB volume fraction, the shear modulus is reduced to approximately 1/2 of the neat matrix while the bulk modulus is less than 1% of the neat matrix value' (fully crushed), and 'with fcrush = 0.05 it is only 12-16% of its undamaged value'. Since bulk and shear moduli have no dedicated schema fields and the multipliers are explicitly approximate, no 'model' records were created; these figures are flagged here instead. (3) The 20% modulus reduction in compression and 40% in tension for debonded GMBs in a glassy matrix (Em = 3.2 GPa) is quoted from Cho et al. [7] and concerns a different, unspecified material, so it was not recorded as a secondary datum. (4) The remark that matrix micro-cracking is absent until global failure near 70% compressive engineering strain comes from the authors' related synchrotron work (Patterson et al. [33]) and is not tied to a specific composition here, so no strain_at_failure was recorded. (5) No densities, strengths, or energy-absorption values are reported anywhere in the paper.
